subfield: surfaces of revolution, apparent contours, evolutes
modern_restatement_en: Let $S$ be a surface of revolution about the $z$-axis and $v$ a direction oblique to the axis. Let $\Gamma\subset S$ be the contact curve of the cylinder with generators parallel to $v$ circumscribed about $S$. The horizontal segments joining points of $\Gamma$ to the axis form a conoid $R$; let $Z$ be the cylinder with generators parallel to $v$ circumscribed about $R$. Then in a plane perpendicular to the axis, the section of $Z$ is the evolute of the section of the first cylinder.
well_posed_note: The cutting plane is unspecified. The statement holds for planes perpendicular to the axis, but fails in general. For a sphere cut by a plane perpendicular to $v$, the first section is a circle, whose evolute is a point, while the second contour is the evolute of an ellipse. Degenerate when $v$ is parallel or perpendicular to the axis.

elementary_check.plan: Project along $v=(\sin\varphi,0,\cos\varphi)$ onto $z=0$. For meridian $r=f(z)$, contact points satisfy $\cos\theta=f'(z)\cot\varphi$. The projected rulings join $\pi(P)$ to $\pi(Q)$, $Q=(0,0,z)$, and the second contour is their envelope. It equals the evolute iff these lines are normal to the projected curve, i.e. the tangent dot product is 0 (analytically it is $f\,(f'-\tan\varphi\cos\theta)=0$). PASS if the maximum normalized dot product is below $10^{-6}$.
elementary_check.code:
import math
phi=0.7
f=lambda z:2+0.3*math.cos(z)+0.1*z
fp=lambda z:-0.3*math.sin(z)+0.1
def Pp(z):
    th=math.acos(fp(z)/math.tan(phi))
    return (f(z)*math.cos(th)-z*math.tan(phi),f(z)*math.sin(th))
def Qp(z): return (-z*math.tan(phi),0.0)
worst=0
for i in range(1,100):
    z=-2+4*i/100;h=1e-6
    p1,p2=Pp(z-h),Pp(z+h);T=((p2[0]-p1[0])/(2*h),(p2[1]-p1[1])/(2*h))
    P,Q=Pp(z),Qp(z);N=(P[0]-Q[0],P[1]-Q[1])
    c=abs(T[0]*N[0]+T[1]*N[1])/(math.hypot(*T)*math.hypot(*N));worst=max(worst,c)
print('PASS' if worst<1e-6 else 'FAIL','projected rulings are normals of section (plane perpendicular to axis)',worst)

belief.note: No published solution is known to me. It is true for sections perpendicular to the axis, by a two-line computation: the projected rulings are the normals of the first section, so their envelope is its evolute. It is false for other cutting planes.
